title: Least Privilege Workflows and SIEM Contracts
body:
Purpose and scope:
This document describes a pragmatic, environment-aware least-privilege model (RBAC v2) and the log/telemetry contract for forwarding audit events to customer SIEMs and internal detection pipelines. It focuses on three deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and covers: role and workflow definitions, onboarding/offboarding flows, example policy snippets, audit-log schema, SIEM export mapping, and evidence automation hooks for access reviews and compliance checks.

Design principles (short):
- Principle of least privilege per deployment-mode: only grant the minimal action-level permissions required for a task.
- Separation of duties: administrative operations versus application/runtime roles are distinct.
- Auditable actions: every privilege escalation, secret access, and deployment action must emit a structured audit event.
- Machine-friendly audit schema: logs need stable field names and typed values to support deterministic SIEM parsing and evidence automation.
- Privacy-safe: PII must be redacted before export to customer SIEMs unless approved and documented.

Stakeholders:
- Security & Compliance (owner): defines RBAC v2 shape and audit schema.
- Platform Engineering: implements enforcement hooks, policy templates, and runtime checks.
- SRE/Infra: configures SIEM export pipelines and retention.
- Product/Customer Success: validates customer requirements for Dedicated/Private exports.
- Legal/Privacy: approves any PII forwarding.

High-level RBAC v2 constructs (plain language):
- Role templates: coarse named templates that map to action sets (not raw cloud primitives). Examples: read-only-audit, model-deployer, runtime-operator, infra-operator, billing-viewer, security-auditor, support-agent.
- Role bindings: attach role templates to subjects (users, service principals, groups) scoped to an environment and optionally scoped to resources (model namespace, customer account).
- Privilege paths: short-lived elevation request flows for emergency or maintenance tasks (timeboxed approvals, automatic revocation).
- Policy derivation: roles are compiled into provider-specific IAM policies (cloud or on-prem). The compilation step should be deterministic and reversible for audits.

Environment-specific guidance (summary):
1) Hosted (multi-tenant, Redwood-managed control plane):
- Minimize access: internal teams should rarely have direct access to customer data. Roles should be namespaced to internal services.
- Customer access: customers receive service-level control (API keys, API-level role bindings) but not cloud resource credentials.
- Audit volume: high; sampling strategies allowed for debug-level traces but core audit events must be complete.
- SIEM export: expose aggregated meta-events to customers (per contract). PII redaction by default.

2) Dedicated (Redwood-managed, isolated infra for a customer):
- Strong resource scoping: roles must be scoped to the dedicated cluster or GPU pool.
- Operator roles: platform engineering and customer operator roles must be clearly separated.
- Evidence requirements: scheduled access reviews every 30 days; automation must produce a snapshot of bindings plus proof of removal.
- SIEM export: full-event forwarding enabled per contract; ensure encryption-in-transit for exported streams.

3) Private (customer-managed control plane / VPC / on-prem):
- Default: Redwood’s control plane access minimized; customer owns most operational access.
- Administrative access: Redwood support may have a limited support role for diagnostics; must be timeboxed and require customer consent or a ticket.
- Audit posture: Redwood should provide a local agent that emits the standard audit schema; customers must map to their SIEM.
- SIEM export: typically controlled by customer; provide guidelines and a reference parser.

Role examples and allowed action sets (human-readable table as text):
- read-only-audit: list/read metadata for models, deployments, configs. Cannot access secrets or logs with PII.
- model-deployer: create/update model bundles, start/stop endpoints, view model metrics. Cannot modify infra nodes or billing settings.
- runtime-operator: manage runtime configuration (batching/caching), restart runtime processes, view runtime logs excluding raw user payloads.
- infra-operator: modify node pools, scale GPU clusters, change kernel-level settings; sensitive and limited to infra team and approved customer operators.
- security-auditor: read access to full audit stream, ability to create investigation tickets; cannot change runtime or infra state.
- support-agent: scoped to a customer account, can run a narrow set of diagnostic commands via 'support session' which are time-limited and produce an automated audit bundle.

Onboarding flow (short):
1) Request: team requests role via internal access portal (link to ticket).
2) Approval: role owner approves (or SSO group membership verifies).
3) Binding creation: automated compilation converts the template binding into runtime IAM policy and attaches it.
4) Evidence: system emits an audit event 'binding.created' with policy snapshot and ticket ID.
5) Periodic review: reviewer receives automatic digest with 'who has access' and 'how were privileges used' (last 90 days).

Offboarding / emergency revocation: steps:
- Automated IAM revoke endpoint: immediately remove bindings for specified subjects and emit 'binding.revoked' with requestor, reason, and ticket id.
- If support session in progress, session is terminated and session transcript is sealed for audit.
- Post-mortem: 72-hour required SRM (security review meeting) for any emergency elevation.

Audit log schema (canonical JSON fields, example described as key: type - all fields are strings or simple primitives in the stream):
Important guidance: logs MUST be emitted as JSON objects (one per line) with stable keys. Field names below are the canonical contract names and should be present for all privilege-related events.
- event_time: ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g., 2025-02-28T15:12:07Z)
- event_type: short token describing action (e.g., binding.created, binding.revoked, deployment.start, model.upload, secret.access, support.session.start)
- request_id: uuid correlator for the request
- actor_id: unique internal id for principal (user/service)
- actor_email: human email when applicable (redact local-part when exporting to customer SIEM unless approved)
- actor_roles: comma-separated list of active role templates at time of event
- resource_type: enum (model, endpoint, cluster, secret, billing_account, audit_snapshot)
- resource_id: opaque identifier (namespaced)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- action_result: success | failure | partial
- client_ip: IP address (masked to /24 when forwarding externally by default)
- geo: country code when available (optional)
- change_summary: short human string describing the change (max 1024 chars)
- policy_snapshot: base64-encoded policy JSON when event_type in [binding.created, binding.updated] (optional for hosted; required for Dedicated evidence exports)
- pii_redaction: boolean (true if PII was redacted from event)
- raw_payload_hash: sha256 of redacted raw payload for tamper-evidence
- detection_tags: comma-separated list for downstream enrichment (e.g., privilege-elevation, admin-action)

Note on sizes and sampling: debug-level events (e.g., per-token traces) should be samplable and flagged event_type=trace; core audit events must not be sampled.

SIEM export contract (for customers and internal ops):
- Transport: JSON-over-TLS to customer SIEM ingestion endpoint (syslog-over-TLS or HTTPS). Deliver events with persistent ack and retry.
- Envelope: each exported line is the canonical JSON schema above. If using syslog, the syslog message body contains the JSON object.
- Field mapping guidance: provide a one-to-one mapping table in onboarding package (we will supply a CSV mapping from Redwood fields to Splunk/QRadar/Elastic fields).
- Redaction policy: by default redact PII (email local-part, query payloads, raw user prompts). Customers can opt-in after Data Processing Agreement amendment.
- Retention and replay: Redwood retains a shelved copy for 90 days for Dedicated customers to support evidence requests; hosted customers get 30 days by default. Replay of events for evidence requests must be timeboxed and logged.
- Rate and throttling: export streams have per-customer quotas to protect SIEM ingestion; provide burst allowances for incident windows.

Detection & evidence automation hooks (how to wire audits into ticketing and access reviews):
- Event subscriptions: internal apps subscribe to particular event_types (e.g., secret.access, binding.created).
- Automated evidence bundle: on access review cycles, system compiles a signed snapshot: list of bindings, policy_snapshots (base64), recent relevant events (last 90 days), and a signed manifest (sha256). Delivered to reviewers and attached to the review ticket.
- Automated checks: rules run weekly to flag stale high-privilege bindings (no use in 30 days), and to open a JIRA if binding.owner is unknown.
- Proof-of-removal: when a binding is revoked, the evidence automation must attach a binding.revoked event + an end-to-end policy diff to the ticket.

Sample policy snippets (human-readable examples; adapt per provider):
- Minimal model-deployer (pseudo-JSON snippet):
  {
    "effect": "allow",
    "actions": ["models:list", "models:create", "deployments:start", "deployments:stop"],
    "resources": ["rn:models:customer-123:*"]
  }

- Support session guard (pseudo-JSON):
  {
    "effect": "allow",
    "actions": ["support:session:start"],
    "conditions": {"timebox_expires_at": "2025-03-01T15:00:00Z", "ticket_id": "JIRA-9999"}
  }

Privacy notes (forwarding to customer SIEMs):
- Default: redact user prompt content and any PII before exporting.
- If customer requests full payloads for Dedicated/Private, require a signed DPA addendum and explicit logging consent.
- Preserve hashed fingerprints of payloads (raw_payload_hash) to allow correlation without exposing content.

Operational playbooks (short pointers):
- On suspected privilege abuse: mark actor_id, freeze bindings, capture full audit slice (with policy_snapshots), notify security-auditor role, open high-priority investigation ticket.
- For evidence requests: compile signed bundle, run a tamper-check (compare raw_payload_hash chain), produce a replay window, and mark exported bundles with the approver and timestamp.

Appendix: minimal checklists and good practices (bulleted):
- Use role templates, avoid ad-hoc policy edits.
- Prefer group bindings over individual user bindings.
- Enforce MFA for all admin or operator roles.
- Timebox any elevation and record the reason and approver.
- Keep policy_snapshots with every binding change for forensics.
- Retain audit artifacts long enough to satisfy customer or regulatory SLA; follow the default retention rules above.

Open questions / next steps (work-in-progress items to resolve):
- Standardized token for cross-customer request correlation (proposal: rwd-request-id).
- Exact retention windows for high-sensitivity customers (legal to finalize).
- Packaging a Redwood-to-SIEM reference parser for three major SIEMs (Elastic, Splunk, QRadar) as a supported repo.
- Automating DPA addendum triggering on customer opt-ins for full payload forwarding.

Document history:
- 2024-09-18: Draft created by Aisha Patel.
- 2024-10-30: Added policy snapshot requirement for Dedicated exports (Marco Chen).
- 2025-02-28: Clarified export redaction and retention rules (Lina Gomez).

References and links:
- Confluence: RBAC v2 design (confluence://SEC/rbac-v2-design)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4123 (RBAC v2 rollout)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR/893 (export pipeline change)
